forces.title: Rising energy prices and geopolitical disruption increase operational costs
forces.description: The Middle East conflict and global energy market volatility have led to significantly higher oil, gas, and electricity prices across Europe. This directly increases operational costs for Facilities & Support Services providers, particularly for energy-intensive building operations and food procurement in institutional catering. Clients, facing similar cost pressures, will demand greater efficiency, squeezing F&SS margins if cost increases cannot be fully passed through. The prolonged nature of geopolitical instability maintains this high-impact risk.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Increasing labor costs and workforce shortages challenge operations
forces.description: Ireland faces significant labor market challenges, including rising minimum wages, inflationary pressures on payroll, and acute shortages of personnel across service sectors. Specifically, recruitment difficulties for skilled workers such as chefs and electricians directly impact institutional catering and building operations within F&SS. These factors elevate operational costs for F&SS providers, making it difficult to maintain margins and meet service delivery requirements without investing in efficiency improvements or automation. The issue is structural, with no immediate resolution.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Client focus on operational efficiency and cost control intensifies
forces.description: Clients across key F&SS end-markets, including healthcare, hospitality, and food & beverage, are experiencing severe margin pressure from rising input and labor costs. This necessitates an intensified focus on operational efficiency and cost control. Consequently, F&SS providers are facing increased demand to deliver solutions that reduce client expenses, optimize processes, and provide clear value. This structural shift requires F&SS firms to offer more data-driven, efficient, and potentially tech-enabled services to remain competitive and support client profitability.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Growing demand for energy-efficient building solutions
forces.description: High energy prices, coupled with increasingly stringent climate policies and ESG investor demands, are driving a strong and growing preference for energy-efficient buildings across residential, commercial, and healthcare sectors. This creates a significant tailwind for Facilities & Support Services, particularly in building operations and integrated facilities management. Demand for services related to energy efficiency upgrades, retrofits, and sustainable building management is expected to remain resilient as property owners and investors seek to reduce operational costs, enhance asset value, and meet regulatory/ESG targets.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Increased investment in building maintenance, upgrades, and refurbishment
forces.description: Despite low activity in new building construction in Norway, there is a notable pickup in operation and maintenance (O&M) activity. Both private and public sectors are prioritizing upgrades, rehabilitation, and maintenance of existing infrastructure over new builds. This shift provides a strong tailwind for Facilities & Support Services specializing in building operations, maintenance contracts, and facility improvement projects. It helps offset the dampening effect of weak new construction and ensures continued demand for core F&SS offerings.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Acceleration of AI and automation adoption across client sectors
forces.description: The widespread adoption of AI and automation technologies is accelerating across various client sectors, including food & beverage, hospitality, and healthcare. This trend is driven by the need to improve productivity, streamline operations, and offset labor shortages. For Facilities & Support Services, this represents a significant structural change. While some tasks may be automated, it also creates an upside driver for F&SS providers who can integrate and offer tech-enabled solutions for administrative efficiency, rostering, energy monitoring, and other back-office and operational processes, enhancing their value proposition.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Stricter regulatory and ESG demands drive compliance and sustainability services
forces.description: New EU regulations, such as the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), enhanced food safety regulations, and restrictions on chemicals in food contact packaging, are increasing compliance burdens. Concurrently, investor and client focus on ESG factors (e.g., decarbonization strategies, waste reduction) is intensifying. This structural change creates a robust upside driver for Facilities & Support Services. Providers capable of offering compliance support, sustainable packaging solutions, waste management, and energy efficiency upgrades are well-positioned to meet these evolving client and regulatory demands, embedding sustainability as a core service offering.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Weak new construction activity dampens demand for F&SS in new builds
forces.description: Low numbers of new-builds in both commercial and residential construction, particularly in Norway, continue to dampen growth in the construction sector. This trend is primarily attributed to higher interest rates and rising building costs, leading to project postponements. For Facilities & Support Services, this acts as a headwind by reducing demand for initial facilities setup, building commissioning, and integrated facilities management for new properties. The sector must adapt by focusing more on maintenance and upgrades of existing assets to mitigate this impact.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

forces.title: VAT rate reduction for Irish food services improves profitability outlook
forces.description: The Irish government's decision to introduce a 9% food-services VAT rate, effective July 2026, is expected to be welcomed by the hospitality sector, which has faced sustained margin pressure. This reduction creates a tailwind for institutional catering within Facilities & Support Services, as it can alleviate some of the cost burdens for their clients in food-led businesses. Improved profitability for hospitality clients may lead to more stable or increased demand for catering services, enhancing the financial outlook for F&SS providers in this segment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Increasing data centre buildout drives demand for specialized facilities management
forces.description: Norway is experiencing increased data centre buildout, leading to higher demand for energy supply equipment and, implicitly, for the specialized Facilities & Support Services required to manage these complex, high-tech infrastructures. Data centres necessitate comprehensive integrated facilities management, including advanced building operations, energy management, and specialized support services. This trend represents a significant upside driver for F&SS providers capable of meeting the stringent operational and technical demands of the rapidly expanding data centre market, contributing to growth in the commercial services sector.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Healthcare client cost pressures and capacity constraints drive F&SS demand for efficiency
viewpoints.description: Ireland's healthcare sector, a significant client for Facilities & Support Services (F&SS) providers in areas like building operations and institutional catering, faces ongoing pressure from rising payroll, regulatory, and operational costs. Despite strong demand and robust investment activity in nursing homes and disability services, providers struggle with profitability. This environment compels healthcare facilities to seek greater cost efficiency from their F&SS partners, creating opportunities for service providers who can deliver value, tech-enabled solutions, and support facility upgrades over new builds.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Hospitality clients prioritize cost control and tech, shaping F&SS opportunities
viewpoints.description: The Irish hospitality sector, a key client for institutional catering and building operations, exhibits rate-led growth but faces margin pressure from persistent cost inflation, especially in food services. Operators are intensifying focus on controlling input costs, adopting energy efficiency measures, and leveraging AI/automation for operational friction reduction. This shifts F&SS demand towards providers who can offer data-driven solutions, support refurbishment/upgrades, and enable a smaller, more skilled workforce to enhance client profitability and service quality.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Growing value premium for energy-efficient homes boosts building operations services
viewpoints.description: The Belgian housing market shows a growing 'value premium' for energy-efficient homes due to higher energy prices and stringent renovation requirements. This trend significantly elevates the importance of energy performance in property value and marketability. For Facilities & Support Services, particularly building operations and integrated facilities management, this represents a positive outlook. Demand is expected to remain resilient for services related to insulation, high-performance glazing, and efficient heating systems, as these investments offer financial benefits and hedge against future energy price shocks.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Commercial real estate ESG focus drives demand for sustainable building operations
viewpoints.description: The Dutch commercial real estate market, despite a strong Q1, faces headwinds from rising costs, execution bottlenecks, and geopolitical uncertainty. Institutional investors are increasingly prioritizing societal impact, ESG policies, and sustainability pathways, leading to declining interest in outdated buildings. However, operation and maintenance activity is picking up. This creates a cautious positive outlook for Facilities & Support Services, particularly for providers specializing in sustainable building operations, energy transition upgrades, and retrofitting existing assets to meet evolving environmental standards and investor demands.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Services sector faces mixed labor outlook, AI dampens demand for entry-level roles
viewpoints.description: Norway's services sector, which includes Facilities & Support Services, expects overall output growth. However, there's a mixed outlook for employment. While overall employment is projected to edge up, some consultancy firms report reduced recruitment, partly due to increased AI adoption dampening labor demand, especially for entry-level positions. Recruitment difficulties persist for skilled workers like chefs and electricians, directly impacting institutional catering and building operations. This suggests a need for F&SS providers to adapt workforce strategies, leverage technology, and address specific skill shortages to manage operational demands.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Rising agricultural input costs squeeze institutional catering margins in Ireland
viewpoints.description: The Irish agriculture sector faces a challenging outlook for 2026, with rising input costs (fertilizer, fuel, energy) driven by geopolitical conflicts and adverse weather impacting production. This leads to higher food production costs and squeezed farm profitability across dairy, beef, sheep, and pigs. For institutional catering services within Facilities & Support Services, this implies a negative impact due to increased raw material costs. Providers will need to carefully manage procurement and pricing to maintain margins in an environment of elevated food inflation.
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

viewpoints.title: F&B sector faces cost pressures and regulatory changes, driving F&SS efficiency demand
viewpoints.description: The Irish Food & Beverage sector, a key client for institutional catering, is shaped by global conflict, high input costs, supply chain disruption, and new EU regulations (packaging, food safety). Food inflation remains a concern, and sustainability goals necessitate robust decarbonization strategies. This presents a cautious outlook for institutional catering, which must manage rising raw material costs and increased compliance burdens. However, it also creates opportunities for F&SS providers offering solutions in automation, operational efficiency, waste management, and regulatory compliance to support their F&B clients.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Increased O&M activity offsets low new-builds in commercial real estate
viewpoints.description: Norway's commercial real estate (CRE) sector reports stable turnover and leasing, with customers becoming more cautious and cost-conscious. While new building construction remains low, there's a notable increase in operation and maintenance (O&M) activity. Both private and public sectors are prioritizing upgrades over new-builds, driven by existing investment backlogs. This outlook is positive for Facilities & Support Services focused on building operations, maintenance, and rehabilitation, as demand shifts from new construction projects to enhancing and upgrading existing infrastructure.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

demand_drivers.description: Healthcare and hospitality clients are prioritizing energy efficiency upgrades and refurbishment over new builds, driven by high energy costs and ESG considerations, creating demand for F&SS in building operations.

Clients in healthcare, hospitality, and food & beverage face margin pressure from rising labor and input costs, increasing their demand for F&SS that can deliver operational efficiencies and cost savings.

Clients are investing in automation, digitalization, and AI to improve productivity and manage costs, creating opportunities for F&SS providers who can offer tech-enabled integrated facilities management solutions.

pnl_drivers.description: Minimum wage increases, broader inflationary pressures on payroll, and workforce shortages across the services sector (including for skilled workers like chefs and electricians) directly increase F&SS operating expenses.

Geopolitical conflicts leading to higher oil, gas, and related energy prices, along with increased agricultural input costs (fertilizer, fuel), significantly raise operational costs for F&SS, particularly for institutional catering and building operations.

new_opportunities.description: Increasing client and investor focus on ESG, energy transition, and stricter climate policies creates demand for F&SS providers specializing in energy efficiency upgrades, sustainable building operations, and compliance with new regulations (e.g., packaging waste).

The acceleration of AI and automation adoption in client sectors presents an opportunity for F&SS to integrate digital solutions for administrative efficiency, rostering, energy monitoring, and other back-office processes, improving productivity and service quality.

Weak new construction activity in some regions, coupled with a client shift towards improving existing facilities, refurbishment, and routine maintenance, offers growth opportunities for F&SS in building operations and integrated facilities management.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Refurbishment and maintenance over new builds

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of key demand and P&L drivers for Facilities & Support Services based on trends in client sectors (healthcare, hospitality, food & beverage) and broader economic conditions in Ireland.

demand_drivers.description: In commercial real estate, despite low new construction, there is a clear shift towards prioritizing upgrades, rehabilitation, and maintenance of existing buildings, directly driving demand for F&SS building operations.
The ongoing expansion of data centres is creating significant demand for related energy supply equipment and, implicitly, for integrated facilities management to support these complex operations.
Increased government spending in defence and emergency preparedness boosts activity in commercial services, which can include various support services within F&SS.

pnl_drivers.description: The services sector faces persistent challenges in recruiting skilled workers such as chefs and electricians, leading to higher labor costs and operational constraints for institutional catering and building operations.
Geopolitical uncertainty, cost growth, and higher interest rates are making clients more hesitant, potentially halting or postponing projects, thus impacting F&SS revenue and project pipeline.

new_opportunities.description: As digital solutions reduce the need for some employees and AI integration improves productivity, F&SS providers can offer tech-enabled services to optimize operations, reduce costs, and address labor challenges.
new_opportunities.opportunity: AI and digital solutions for efficiency
